title: Model run manifest
description: How a computed 3D object was made: what data went in, with which settings, by which script, in which environment, what came out and which checks it passed. Filed with the object so that anyone with a code sandbox can run the same recipe again on current data. geoDB checks the structure and the file hashes; it never judges the content and never executes a recipe.

manifest_version.description: The version of this contract. Always 1.

kind.description: What the run made. A mesh layer takes grade_shell, surface or solid.

title.description: A short name for the result, as a person would say it.

made_by.description: The program or AI that made it, with its version, as it reports itself.

replaces.description: The id of the mesh layer this run is the next version of, or null.

inputs.description: Every pull the recipe makes, so the same pull can be made again.

what.description: What was pulled, in plain words.

read.description: The API read it came from (a path under /api/v2/).

filters.description: The query parameters of that read, as sent.

fields.description: The fields of each pulled row the recipe uses, which are the fields the fingerprint covers.

fingerprint.description: To tell later whether the data changed. Keep only `fields` of each pulled row; write each row as JSON with its keys sorted, no whitespace (separators "," and ":") and non-ASCII characters escaped; sort those row texts; join them with "," between "[" and "]"; the fingerprint is the SHA-256 of that text (UTF-8), as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

set.description: For "what": "interpretation constraints" (modelling phase 3): the id of the constraint set read (GET /api/v2/constraint-sets/). It must be a live set of this project; record the set's served `fingerprint` beside it.

parameters.description: Every setting the recipe takes (cutoff and its units, composite length, grid size and so on). The recipe reads its settings from here and from nowhere else.

file.description: The recipe's file name (a plain .py name).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact bytes, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

entry.description: How to run it, for example "python recipe.py".

environment.description: The interpreter and package versions the run used, for example {"python": "3.12", "packages": {"scipy": "1.16.2"}}.

role.description: What the file is. "mesh" is the .glb a mesh layer draws.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact bytes, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

length_unit.description: The unit of X, Y and Z in the file.

checks.description: The checks the maker ran on the result, each with its outcome.

caveats.description: What the result is not. Always present, for example "An interpolated surface for visualisation, not a mineral resource estimate."
